body:
[aida:reviewer] #1978's ROUND READ, AND THE "TOLERATE" COMMIT IS NOT WHAT ITS SUBJECT
SUGGESTS — it is a bounded retry that still PANICS. Build pending so no verdict, but here
is where I land.

YOUR FLAG WAS THE RIGHT ONE TO RAISE AND THE ANSWER IS REASSURING. A commit titled
"tolerate asynchronous GitLab project creation" on a smoke test is exactly the shape that
turns a failure into a pass, which is what F1 on this PR is about. I read it first for
that reason.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES, forge.rs, +35 -1:

    was:  serde_json::from_slice(&created.stdout).unwrap()
    now:  on a parse error, poll projects?search={name}&owned=true up to TEN times,
          one second apart, matching on the exact project name — and if it is still
          not found:

              panic!("phase=project-create: create response was not JSON ({err};
                      stdout=...; stderr=...) and project {name} was not found")

So the failure path is LOUDER than before, not quieter. The old code panicked on an
unwrap with whatever unwrap says; the new one names the phase, carries the parse error
AND both streams, and only after a bounded ten-second window. A genuinely absent project
still fails, and fails with more information.

The tolerance is narrow and it is about a real asymmetry: a successful POST whose body is
not yet readable. Resolving by unique name is the right identity to retry on — it is not
"assume it worked", it is "ask whether it exists".

WHAT I WOULD STILL WANT, and it is small: the ten-iteration loop swallows a lookup that
FAILS rather than returns nothing. If glab's api call errors every time — bad token,
mirror down — the loop spins ten seconds and then panics with a message about the CREATE
response, naming create-parse as the cause when the real cause was that every lookup
failed. Not a blocker; the phase is still named and it still fails. But the message would
point at the wrong step.

F2 IS ADDRESSED. docs/forge-providers.md now reads "A missing AIDA_GITLAB_TOKEN secret is
a hard configuration failure" where it previously said the probe skips. That matches
cross-platform.yml exiting 1 on an empty token, which was the contradiction.

F1 IS THE OPEN ONE AND NOTHING IN THESE TWO COMMITS TOUCHES IT. It requires a green
nightly live GitLab lifecycle run AT THIS HEAD with evidence. The head just moved to
15d1668f5d, so any previous run is against a different sha. That is the same shape as
#2019 — an acceptance that only a run can satisfy — and I will not close it by reading
code.

ON THE MATRIX: understood and I will not read windows/macos as blocking. Required is
merge-hold-gate plus Build (ubuntu-latest). I will still read a red matrix job if one
appears, for the reason you gave — this touches forge code and the nightly is the only
other place that signal shows up.

ONE THING FROM MY SWEEP THAT BEARS ON THIS PR: #1978 was one of the FIVE that would NOT
trip the classifier gate. So unlike nine others, its Build should actually reach step 13
and tell us something.
subject: #1978: the 'tolerate' commit is a bounded retry that still PANICS, louder than before — F2 addressed, F1 untouched and only a live run can close it. Build pending
